concepts.definition: Read broadly: public, private, non-profit and social enterprises of every size and structure, from start-ups and micro businesses to global firms; business likewise is read broadly (D1, 1.9)
concepts.beneficiaryDefinition: Any kind of organisation you might work in, from a start-up or charity to a public body or a global company.

concepts.definition: Leadership that is authentic, driven by values, inclusive, ethical, sustainable, systemic and transformative, weighing stakeholders now and in future and addressing climate change and fair, inclusive net zero (D1, 1.10)
concepts.beneficiaryDefinition: Leading in a way that is ethical, inclusive and sustainable, and that thinks about everyone affected, now and later.

concepts.definition: Building professional-level knowledge and skills, or preparing for research and further study, with self-awareness, personal development and a positive stance on change and enterprise (D1, 1.11)
concepts.beneficiaryDefinition: Getting ready for, or moving on in, a business career, or preparing for research.

concepts.definition: Transferable academic and professional skills suited to a business career but not limited to it, with continuing reflection, self-awareness, lifelong learning and regard for others' well-being (D1, 1.12)
concepts.beneficiaryDefinition: The skills and qualities you build that are useful in business and beyond it.

concepts.definition: Four course types: Type 1 generalist for career entry, Type 2 generalist for career development (MBA, MPA), Type 3 specialist for career entry, Type 4 specialist for career development (D1, 1.3; 1.20 to 1.30)
concepts.beneficiaryDefinition: Whether a course is broad or specialist, and whether it is for people starting a career or already working.
concepts.scopeNote: the statement treats the types as guidance, not strict categories (1.1)

concepts.definition: A substantial final piece of independent work involving research, such as a dissertation, thesis, consultancy project, white paper or business project (D1, 1.17)
concepts.beneficiaryDefinition: A large final project of your own, such as a dissertation or a consultancy report.
concepts.scopeNote: a characteristic of the taught master's

terms.form: 'Preparation for, and/or further development of, a career in business and management'

digest.definition: Taught master's in the subject vary widely in content, in how many disciplines they draw on and in the perspectives they take, and are often fast-paced, broad or specialist
distinctiveFeatures: Taught master's in the subject vary widely in content, in how many disciplines they draw on and in the perspectives they take, and are often fast-paced, broad or specialist
Every course joins theory to the consideration of practice, with theory preparing students to tackle complex issues and act on opportunities
A capstone project, from a dissertation to a consultancy project or white paper, is a defining feature, with methods training to prepare for it
The discipline changes quickly, and course design and delivery are to follow that change
Courses fall into four types by content (generalist or specialist) and by career stage (entry or development), and a title alone does not fix the type
Courses are interdisciplinary, drawing on social sciences, humanities and sciences, and are designed to join subject knowledge to responsible, effective working
Responsible management, sustainability and inclusion are designed into courses, which cover private, public and non-profit organisations
The subject is closely tied to practice and to employability, with skills developed for and assessed through practice

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: Inclusion is framed by why, what and how the subject is taught: future managers and leaders carry EDI into organisations, content draws on diverse and critical perspectives, and teaching, modes and assessment are inclusive (D1, 1.31 to 1.37)

Accessibility runs from pre-application to after graduation, at least to the regulatory minimum, with barriers designed out and equal access to placements, international and digital learning (D1, 1.38 to 1.40)

Sustainable management, carbon literacy and responsible leadership are built into every functional area, drawing on the SDGs and PRME, with ethics, responsibility and sustainability as a knowledge area (D1, 1.41 to 1.44; 3.10)

Enterprise and entrepreneurship education, joined to employability, builds entrepreneurial mindsets for new ventures and innovation in existing organisations, through theory and experiential learning (D1, 1.45 to 1.49; 3.10; 3.15)

subjectSpecific.text: You may study ethics, responsibility and sustainability in depth: how to manage responsibly and lead ethically on social, legal, economic and environmental questions.
You may study markets and economies in depth, including why markets sometimes fail and what fair trade means.
You may study marketing, sales, negotiation and customers in depth, from consumer behaviour to how products and services are positioned and improved.
You may study finance and accounting in depth: where money comes from, how it is managed and how accounting supports planning, decisions and managing risk.
You may study people and organisational behaviour in depth, including inclusive leadership, managing and developing people, employment law and working across cultures.
You may study operations and innovation in depth, from supply chains and quality to managing projects and using data to support decisions.
You may study data analytics, digital business and information systems in depth, and how they help organisations decide on the basis of evidence.
You may study business policy and strategy in depth, including how organisations plan for risk, crises and continuity.
You may study how public services and charities are run, including their governance, money, leadership and public value.
You may study entrepreneurship in depth: turning new ideas into products, services or organisations, and protecting and valuing intellectual property.
You will gain knowledge of your specialist subject and see how it fits into the wider organisation and its setting.
You will learn the current issues and debates in your specialism and the research techniques used in it.
You will gain both theory and practice so that you can use your specialist skills in the organisations where you may work.
You will be able to manage people: build and motivate teams, choose how to lead in different situations, support well-being and inclusion, and coach others.
You will be able to work out the cause of a problem, weigh possible solutions, choose sustainable ones, test the reasoning behind them and review how they worked.
You will be able to plan and carry out research, analyse numbers and words, report what you find, and judge how sound and relevant published research is.
You will understand what makes a business succeed or fail and why keeping customers satisfied and loyal, in sustainable ways, matters.
You will be able to act in an enterprising way: come up with ideas, develop and share them, protect intellectual property and win support to deliver results.
You will be able to use numbers and data to estimate, evaluate and model business problems.
You will be able to handle complex, messy problems by questioning assumptions, looking across functions and solving them in a careful but creative way.
You will understand how listening, negotiating, persuading and presenting help you build professional contacts.
You will be able to communicate complex ideas clearly in speech, writing and other media, including business reports.
You will know the current problems and new ideas at the leading edge of business and management and your own specialism.
You will be able to work well in different team roles, make use of what each person brings, negotiate and influence, and lead and develop a team.
You will be able to build working relationships and influence people in private, public and voluntary organisations.
You will be able to take on leadership roles responsibly, see when change is needed, start it and manage it.

transferable.text: You will be able to work with people inside and outside an organisation inclusively and with integrity.
You will be able to communicate in speech, in other non-verbal ways and online.
You will be confident with digital tools and know how to behave well online.
You will be able to think in concepts and systems, think critically, and analyse, combine and judge ideas.
You will be able to help settle disagreements between people.
You will be able to manage yourself: take responsibility, adapt, cope with uncertainty, bounce back, get started on your own and speak up when needed.
You will be able to reflect on yourself, be aware of differences between people and cultures, and keep taking charge of building your skills further.
You will be able to understand and empathise with what others need and act inclusively in different situations.
You will have the qualities and skills to take initiative and personal responsibility at work.
You will be able to keep learning on your own throughout your career and plan and run projects independently at a professional level.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management
Purposes and characteristics of taught master's courses: Purposes

statements.appliesTo: general business and management master's courses
statements.about: covering the purposes of a master's
statements.paraphrase: General master's courses in the subject should cover the purposes listed in 1.8, though the balance will vary with the course type and any professional recognition sought, and the intended learning outcomes will show it.

forPractitioner.text: Check the course against the purposes in 1.8: a general master's should address them, weighting them to its type and to any professional accreditation, and its intended outcomes should make that weighting visible.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management
Purposes and characteristics of taught master's courses: Characteristics

statements.appliesTo: students on Type 1 generalist career-entry courses
statements.about: understanding of business contexts for early contribution
statements.paraphrase: Type 1 courses suit graduates of other subjects with little business experience; their postgraduates will develop a sound grasp of business and organisational contexts and so should be able to contribute early and significantly to an employer.

forPractitioner.text: On a career-entry generalist course, aim for a sound grasp of how organisations work that lets students add value to an employer quickly.

forBeneficiary.text: You will build a sound understanding of how businesses and organisations work, so that you can contribute to an employer early on.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management
Purposes and characteristics of taught master's courses: Characteristics

statements.appliesTo: Type 2 generalist post-experience courses, including the MBA
statements.paraphrase: Type 2 generalist courses serve people with substantial work experience, usually at least two years, and learning should build on it; they stress leadership and strategy and use reflective and peer learning, and MBAs differ from other master's in aims, recruitment and teaching.

forPractitioner.text: For a post-experience generalist course such as an MBA, design learning that builds on what entrants bring from at least two years of work, with leadership, strategy, reflection and peer exchange at its centre.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management
Purposes and characteristics of taught master's courses: Characteristics

statements.appliesTo: Type 3 specialist career-entry courses
statements.paraphrase: Type 3 specialist courses usually rest on strong theory but should also give a range of skills relevant to practice; they seldom need work experience, and some link to professional body qualifications.

forPractitioner.text: In a pre-experience specialist course, pair the theory base with skills students can use in practice, and note any professional body qualification the course connects to.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: the subject area and its courses
statements.paraphrase: Equality, diversity and inclusion reach across many identity characteristics and beyond legal duties to intersections in the student and staff body, and the subject area should make EDI a real concept built into its culture and practice.

forPractitioner.text: Treat equality, diversity and inclusion as part of how the subject is taught and practised, not as a compliance add-on, recognising differences that overlap and go beyond the protected characteristics.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: students of the subject, as future managers and leaders
statements.about: EDI principles carried into management and leadership
statements.paraphrase: Business and management education can help organisations tackle inequality, in line with the UN SDGs, and studying the subject will build the principles of equality, diversity and inclusion into future managers and leaders.

forPractitioner.text: Expect graduates to leave with EDI principles as part of how they will manage and lead; teach the link between inclusion, reflective practice and organisations' work on inequality and the SDGs.

forBeneficiary.text: Your studies will build the principles of equality, diversity and inclusion into how you manage and lead, so that you can help organisations tackle inequality.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: postgraduates and the courses they take
statements.paraphrase: Courses make sure students understand critically how organisations and leaders promote EDI; postgraduates should know the legal duty not to discriminate and be equipped to build inclusive workplaces, and content should be diverse and critical of dominant approaches.

forPractitioner.text: Teach the legal duties on discrimination and the skills to build inclusive workplaces; choose content and cases that draw on varied perspectives, including the Global South and marginalised communities, and examine critically how dominant approaches can exclude.

forBeneficiary.text: You should come to know the law that protects people from discrimination and gain the skills to build inclusive workplaces, studying a wide range of perspectives and questioning approaches that leave people out.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: the design of courses and teaching
statements.about: inclusive design of teaching and assessment
statements.paraphrase: Courses should be designed so students from every background can reach their potential and feel represented; teaching, assessment and modes of learning should reflect inclusive principles and pedagogy aware of EDI.

forPractitioner.text: Design so every student can reach their potential and see themselves in the course: weigh the effects of each mode of study, plan assessment that lets different students succeed, and take account of people's multiple identities.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: course teams
statements.about: continuing review of EDI with students
statements.paraphrase: EDI is continuing work: course teams should reflect regularly on how to strengthen it and, where they can, do so with students; approval of changes may include an equality impact assessment.

forPractitioner.text: Put EDI on the regular review cycle, involve students in it where possible, and consider an equality impact assessment when course changes go for approval.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: courses, from pre-application to after graduation
statements.paraphrase: Accessibility asks whether everyone can understand every part of a course however they meet it; it should at least satisfy regulatory requirements and should run from pre-application information to graduation and beyond, with examples given.

forPractitioner.text: Meet the regulatory minimum for accessibility and go further: check information, curriculum, spaces, resources and assessments at every stage, with reasonable adjustments and attention to barriers such as digital poverty and caring duties.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: the design of courses, modules, teaching and assessment
statements.paraphrase: Courses, modules, teaching and assessment should be designed proactively to build in inclusivity and keep obstacles away from neurodivergent students and those with specific learning difficulties.

forPractitioner.text: Anticipate the needs of neurodivergent students and those with specific learning difficulties at design stage rather than waiting for adjustments to be requested.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: courses and their learning opportunities
statements.about: equal access to work, international and digital learning
statements.paraphrase: Accessibility should cover giving every student the same chances of workplace and international learning and digital access that is inclusive and free of discrimination.

forPractitioner.text: Make placements, international experiences and digital provision open to every student on equal terms.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a master's degree in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: the business and management curriculum
statements.paraphrase: Organisations matter for meeting emissions targets, so future leaders need to be ready to respond to climate challenges; management for economic, social and environmental sustainability is to be built systematically into the curriculum and its functional areas, with example topics.

forPractitioner.text: Build sustainability into each functional area of the curriculum, not one module alone, using topics such as sustainable supply chains, carbon literacy, integrated reporting and responsible leadership.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a master's in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: the design of courses
statements.paraphrase: Flexible approaches let students fit study to their circumstances and may widen access; courses should be designed for inclusivity and may offer varied learning modes and assessment.

forPractitioner.text: Design with inclusivity in mind and consider offering a choice of study modes and assessment so students can fit learning to their circumstances.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a master's in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: degree-awarding bodies and their partners
statements.paraphrase: Awarding bodies and partners gather and analyse information and review courses periodically against external reference points, and students should take part in that monitoring and review, which can also cover EDI.

forPractitioner.text: Involve students in monitoring and periodic review, use this statement among the external reference points, and include equality, diversity and inclusion in what is reviewed.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a master's in Business and Management

statements.appliesTo: higher education providers
statements.paraphrase: Externality is essential to UK quality assurance: providers will use external reviewers in periodic review to bring an outside view and to confirm that threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: Include external reviewers in periodic review to test proposed changes, confirm threshold standards and check that content fits the subject.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: generalist and specialist courses
statements.about: scope of generalist and specialist courses
statements.paraphrase: Generalist courses are expected to give a broad, analytical and joined-up study of business and management across complex organisations; specialist courses will place the specialism in the wider field; the statement matches the FHEQ level 7 and SCQF level 11 descriptors.

forPractitioner.text: In a generalist course, cover organisations broadly, analytically and in an integrated way; in a specialist course, set the specialism in the context of the wider field; read both against the level 7 descriptor.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: graduates of taught master's courses
statements.about: knowledge of organisations, context and management
statements.paraphrase: Graduates will be able to show what they know and understand about organisations, their wider business setting including its environmental and regulatory sides, and how organisations are managed; courses stress change, the future of organisations, risk and impact on society.

forPractitioner.text: Ensure graduates can show knowledge of organisations, their environmental and regulatory context and their management, with attention to change, risk, sustainability and social impact.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to show what you know about organisations, the wider business world they operate in, including its environmental and legal sides, and how they are managed.

statements.appliesTo: successful master's graduates
statements.paraphrase: How the areas named in 3.2 relate and fit together matters greatly, and successful graduates from every mode of study will show it in what they can do.

forPractitioner.text: Teach and assess the links between organisations, their context and their management, not each area alone, whatever the mode of study.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to show how what you know about organisations, their context and their management fits together.

statements.appliesTo: courses and their learning outcomes
statements.about: knowledge and skills set in learning outcomes
statements.paraphrase: Each course's learning outcomes will set out its subject knowledge, understanding and skills, which may differ with the type of master's.

forPractitioner.text: State the course's knowledge, understanding and skills in its learning outcomes, matched to its type in the typology.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: master's graduates
statements.paraphrase: Graduates are typically able to show broad knowledge and deep understanding of organisations, their external context and their management; they will understand change and respond to it, and will have the breadth to connect areas of an organisation, even on specialist courses.

forPractitioner.text: Expect graduates, specialists included, to understand and respond to change and to link the different areas of an organisation, with broad knowledge and deep understanding.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how organisations change and how to respond, and you will be able to connect different parts of an organisation, even if you specialise.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of ethics, responsibility and sustainability: managing responsibly and leading ethically on social, cultural, legal, economic and environmental questions.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of responsible management and ethical leadership across social, legal, economic and environmental issues.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study ethics, responsibility and sustainability in depth: how to manage responsibly and lead ethically on social, legal, economic and environmental questions.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of markets and economies: how markets for resources, goods and services form and work, including market failure, externalities and fair trade.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of how markets develop and operate, including their failures, externalities and fair trade.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study markets and economies in depth, including why markets sometimes fail and what fair trade means.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of marketing, sales, negotiation and customers: customer relationships, consumer behaviour, segmentation, targeting and positioning, sales and innovation in products and services.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of customer relationships, consumer behaviour, segmentation and positioning, selling and product and service innovation.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study marketing, sales, negotiation and customers in depth, from consumer behaviour to how products and services are positioned and improved.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of finance and accounting: where finance comes from and how it is used and managed, and how accounting and information systems serve planning, control, decisions and financial risk.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of sources and uses of finance and of accounting information for planning, control, decisions and risk.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study finance and accounting in depth: where money comes from, how it is managed and how accounting supports planning, decisions and managing risk.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of people and organisational behaviour: responsible and inclusive leadership, strategic people management and development, engagement, the legal context, cross-cultural issues and EDI.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of inclusive leadership, strategic people management, engagement, employment law, cross-cultural working and EDI.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study people and organisational behaviour in depth, including inclusive leadership, managing and developing people, employment law and working across cultures.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of operations and business innovation: resources, supply chains, procurement, logistics, outsourcing, quality, service excellence and projects, and turning data into information for analysis and decisions.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of operations, supply chains, quality and project management, and of tools that turn data into decision support.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study operations and innovation in depth, from supply chains and quality to managing projects and using data to support decisions.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.about: data analytics, digital business and information systems
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of analytics and statistics, digital business, information systems and business intelligence: setting digital priorities and using information systems to support decisions driven by data.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of analytics, statistics, information systems and business intelligence for data-driven decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study data analytics, digital business and information systems in depth, and how they help organisations decide on the basis of evidence.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of business policy and strategy: forming policies and strategies for a changing environment and stakeholders, with risk, crisis and continuity management and communication.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of strategy and policy making for stakeholders, with risk, crisis and continuity planning.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study business policy and strategy in depth, including how organisations plan for risk, crises and continuity.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of public and non-profit strategic management: how public services and the voluntary and community sector work, including governance, finance, leadership, co-production, public value and ethics.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of public and voluntary sector governance, finance, leadership, co-production and public value.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study how public services and charities are run, including their governance, money, leadership and public value.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of generalist courses (Types 1 and 2)
statements.paraphrase: Will typically gain deep knowledge and critical understanding of entrepreneurship and enterprise development: turning innovative ideas into new products, services or organisations that earn a return, including identifying and valuing intellectual property.

forPractitioner.text: Where the course covers it, develop critical understanding of venture creation and of recognising and valuing intellectual property.

forBeneficiary.text: You may study entrepreneurship in depth: turning new ideas into products, services or organisations, and protecting and valuing intellectual property.

statements.appliesTo: MPA courses
statements.paraphrase: MPA courses will give more weight to governance, public policy and public management content.

forPractitioner.text: In an MPA, weight the content towards governance, public policy and public management.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a statement about MPA course content, not an outcome for the student

statements.appliesTo: graduates of specialist courses (Types 3 and 4)
statements.about: the specialist subject in its wider setting
statements.paraphrase: Will acquire knowledge of the specialist subject and set it within its wider organisational and contextual frame.

forPractitioner.text: Develop specialist knowledge and the ability to place the specialism within the wider organisation and its context.

forBeneficiary.text: You will gain knowledge of your specialist subject and see how it fits into the wider organisation and its setting.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of specialist courses (Types 3 and 4)
statements.about: current issues and research techniques in the specialism
statements.paraphrase: Will acquire knowledge of current issues and thinking in the specialist area and of the research techniques used in it.

forPractitioner.text: Cover the specialism's current debates and the research techniques its field uses.

forBeneficiary.text: You will learn the current issues and debates in your specialism and the research techniques used in it.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of specialist courses (Types 3 and 4)
statements.about: theory and application of specialist skills
statements.paraphrase: Will acquire theoretical and applied perspectives that let them use specialist skills in the organisations and settings where they may work.

forPractitioner.text: Combine theory and application so specialists can use their skills in the organisations they are likely to join.

forBeneficiary.text: You will gain both theory and practice so that you can use your specialist skills in the organisations where you may work.

statements.appliesTo: students of Types 2 and 4 career-development courses
statements.about: new knowledge grounded in professional experience
statements.paraphrase: On career-development courses of Types 2 and 4, students will be able to root what they newly learn in their own professional experience.

forPractitioner.text: On post-experience courses, ask students to connect new theory to their own working experience in teaching and assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to connect what you learn to your own experience at work.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.about: cognitive, subject, personal and team skills
statements.paraphrase: Graduates will be able to show cognitive and intellectual skills and business and management competencies, with well-developed personal, interpersonal and teamwork skills that go beyond those of a first degree.

forPractitioner.text: Develop and assess intellectual skills, subject competencies and strong personal, interpersonal and team skills at a level beyond undergraduate study.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to show strong thinking skills, business and management competencies and well-developed personal and team-working skills, beyond what a first degree asks.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to manage people: building teams, resilience and well-being, leading and motivating, choosing a fitting leadership style, fostering EDI, managing performance, setting objectives, coaching and mentoring.

forPractitioner.text: Develop people-management skills from team building and motivation to choosing leadership styles, managing performance, coaching and fostering inclusion.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to manage people: build and motivate teams, choose how to lead in different situations, support well-being and inclusion, and coach others.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to solve problems and analyse critically: gather information, find causes, weigh and choose sustainable solutions, think critically and creatively, test assumptions and logic, and carry out and review decisions.

forPractitioner.text: Develop structured problem-solving and critical analysis: diagnosing causes, evaluating options, choosing sustainable solutions, checking assumptions and reasoning, and reviewing decisions once made.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work out the cause of a problem, weigh possible solutions, choose sustainable ones, test the reasoning behind them and review how they worked.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to research business and management issues alone or in teams: design, collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative data, synthesise and report, with strong digital literacy, and judge the rigour and relevance of published research.

forPractitioner.text: Develop research skills across design, mixed data collection and analysis, synthesis and reporting, with digital literacy, and the critical appraisal of published studies for evidence-based decisions.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to plan and carry out research, analyse numbers and words, report what you find, and judge how sound and relevant published research is.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will have commercial acumen grounded in knowing what drives business success and failure and why sustainable customer satisfaction and loyalty matter.

forPractitioner.text: Develop commercial awareness of what makes organisations succeed or fail and how they keep customers satisfied and loyal in sustainable ways.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand what makes a business succeed or fail and why keeping customers satisfied and loyal, in sustainable ways, matters.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to act entrepreneurially: produce, develop and communicate ideas, handle intellectual property, win support and achieve sustainable results.

forPractitioner.text: Develop enterprising behaviour: generating and pitching ideas, managing intellectual property, building support and delivering sustainable results.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to act in an enterprising way: come up with ideas, develop and share them, protect intellectual property and win support to deliver results.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to use quantitative skills to work with data and to evaluate, estimate and model business problems and processes.

forPractitioner.text: Develop quantitative skills for handling data and for estimating and modelling business problems.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to use numbers and data to estimate, evaluate and model business problems.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to manage complexity: question preconceptions, cross subject and functional boundaries to deal with complex situations as a whole, and solve unstructured problems systematically and creatively.

forPractitioner.text: Develop the ability to work across functional boundaries and solve complex, unstructured problems both systematically and creatively.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to handle complex, messy problems by questioning assumptions, looking across functions and solving them in a careful but creative way.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be aware of the interpersonal skills of listening, negotiation, persuasion and presentation and how they build business contacts.

forPractitioner.text: Develop awareness of listening, negotiating, persuading and presenting as the skills that build professional networks.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how listening, negotiating, persuading and presenting help you build professional contacts.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to communicate complex ideas and arguments verbally and non-verbally through a range of media and technology, including business reports.

forPractitioner.text: Develop communication of complex ideas across media and technologies, including the writing of business reports.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to communicate complex ideas clearly in speech, writing and other media, including business reports.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be aware of current problems and new insights, much of it at or shaped by the forefront of the discipline, a specialism or related professional practice.

forPractitioner.text: Keep students in touch with current problems and new insights from the leading edge of the field and of professional practice.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know the current problems and new ideas at the leading edge of business and management and your own specialism.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to work well in varied team roles, recognise and use members' contributions, negotiate and influence, and select, delegate to, develop and manage a team.

forPractitioner.text: Develop teamwork across roles: drawing on members' contributions, negotiating and influencing, and selecting, delegating to and developing team members.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work well in different team roles, make use of what each person brings, negotiate and influence, and lead and develop a team.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to build relationships and exert influence across private, public and non-profit organisations.

forPractitioner.text: Develop the ability to build relationships and influence across organisations in all three sectors.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to build working relationships and influence people in private, public and voluntary organisations.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to take on leadership roles and fulfil them responsibly and well, seeing when change is needed, starting it and managing it.

forPractitioner.text: Develop responsible leadership, including recognising the need for change, initiating it and managing it through.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to take on leadership roles responsibly, see when change is needed, start it and manage it.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.about: collaborative and inclusive working with stakeholders
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to collaborate inclusively with internal and external stakeholders and with professional integrity.

forPractitioner.text: Develop inclusive collaboration with stakeholders inside and outside the organisation, with professional integrity.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work with people inside and outside an organisation inclusively and with integrity.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to communicate verbally, non-verbally and digitally.

forPractitioner.text: Develop communication in speech, in non-verbal forms and through digital channels.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to communicate in speech, in other non-verbal ways and online.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will have digital literacy and good digital etiquette.

forPractitioner.text: Develop digital literacy and appropriate conduct in digital settings.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be confident with digital tools and know how to behave well online.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to think conceptually, systemically and critically, and to analyse, synthesise and evaluate.

forPractitioner.text: Develop conceptual, systems and critical thinking, with analysis, synthesis and evaluation.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to think in concepts and systems, think critically, and analyse, combine and judge ideas.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to resolve conflict.

forPractitioner.text: Develop the ability to resolve conflict between people and groups.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to help settle disagreements between people.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will manage themselves: taking responsibility, staying flexible and adaptable, coping with uncertainty and complexity, questioning assumptions, being resilient, self-starting and suitably assertive.

forPractitioner.text: Develop self-management: responsibility, adaptability, tolerance of uncertainty, resilience, initiative and appropriate assertiveness.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to manage yourself: take responsibility, adapt, cope with uncertainty, bounce back, get started on your own and speak up when needed.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to reflect on themselves, be aware of and sensitive to diversity in people and cultures, keep wanting to develop and take responsibility for building new skills to a higher level.

forPractitioner.text: Develop self-reflection, sensitivity to diversity and a lasting commitment to building new skills to a higher level.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to reflect on yourself, be aware of differences between people and cultures, and keep taking charge of building your skills further.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will have interpersonal skills: understanding and empathising with others' needs, and sensitivity to diversity and inclusion in different settings.

forPractitioner.text: Develop empathy, understanding of others' needs and sensitivity to diversity and inclusion.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to understand and empathise with what others need and act inclusively in different situations.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will have the qualities and transferable skills for employment that calls for initiative and personal responsibility.

forPractitioner.text: Develop the qualities and transferable skills that roles needing initiative and personal responsibility require.

forBeneficiary.text: You will have the qualities and skills to take initiative and personal responsibility at work.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject's master's courses
statements.paraphrase: Will have the learning ability needed for continuing professional development and be able to plan and deliver projects independently at a professional level.

forPractitioner.text: Develop independent learning for continuing professional development and the ability to plan and run projects alone at professional level.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to keep learning on your own throughout your career and plan and run projects independently at a professional level.

statements.appliesTo: students of Types 2 and 4 career-development courses
statements.paraphrase: Skills differ with course type; on Types 2 and 4, students will be able to learn from earlier experience by reflecting on it, combine new knowledge with it, apply it to new situations and gain new skills while building existing ones.

forPractitioner.text: On career-development courses, build in reflection on prior experience so that students combine it with new knowledge, apply it in new settings and extend their skills.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to reflect on your past experience, combine it with what you learn now, use it in new situations and build both new and existing skills.

statements.appliesTo: assessment and feedback
statements.about: assessment for learning and timely feedback
statements.paraphrase: Assessment should be part of learning, with feedback on formative and summative work that should be timely and usable for development within a module and across the course.

forPractitioner.text: Plan assessment as part of learning and return feedback on both formative and summative work quickly enough, and specifically enough, for students to act on it.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: group assessment
statements.paraphrase: Where work is assessed in groups, the amount of group work, its authenticity, its fit to the task and the split between group and individual marks should all be considered with care.

forPractitioner.text: Decide deliberately how much assessment is group-based, whether the task suits a group, and how group and individual marks are balanced.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: peer review and peer assessment
statements.about: guidance and limits for peer assessment
statements.paraphrase: Peer review and assessment can engage students; whether formative or summative, students should get clear guidance and the weighting of peer assessment in a module should be capped.

forPractitioner.text: When using peer assessment, brief students clearly and cap how much it counts in the module.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: assessment information
statements.paraphrase: Assessment details should be open and given to students with the marking criteria, and there may be room for students to co-design assessments with tutors or peers.

forPractitioner.text: Publish assessment details and marking criteria to students, and consider letting students help design assessments.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: assessment design
statements.paraphrase: Assessment should be planned with the load it places on students in mind.

forPractitioner.text: Check the total assessment load on students when designing assessment, across modules as well as within them.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: higher education providers
statements.about: evidence of achievement above the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Many students will go beyond the threshold; each provider decides what evidence shows this and should refer to the qualification frameworks; the standards match the master's descriptor at FHEQ level 7 and SCQF level 11 and can guide postgraduate certificates and diplomas.

forPractitioner.text: Use the frameworks' master's descriptor when deciding what evidence shows achievement above the threshold, and treat these standards as a reference for postgraduate certificates and diplomas too.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course and its staff; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.about: systematic, deep understanding of organisations and their management
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown a systematic and deep understanding of organisations, their external context and management, and how these relate to each other and to practice.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown systematic, deep understanding of organisations, their context and management, and of how these connect and apply in practice.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown a thorough, organised understanding of organisations, the world around them, how they are run and how all this applies in practice.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.about: understanding of techniques for investigation and research
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown full understanding of the techniques needed for detailed investigation, research or advanced scholarship into issues in business and management or a specialism.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown comprehensive understanding of techniques for detailed investigation, research or advanced scholarship in the field or a specialism.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you understand the methods needed to investigate and research business and management questions in detail.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.about: command of subject and professional skills, with generic skills
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown strong command of the subject's academic and professional skills in the relevant field and steady proficiency in generic skills and attributes.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown a high command of subject-specific academic and professional skills and consistent proficiency in generic skills (see 3.15 and 3.16).

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown a strong command of the academic and professional skills of your field and steady ability in wider, transferable skills.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown critical awareness of current issues in the field, drawn from leading research and practice and from a proactive, independent approach to learning.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown critical awareness of current issues, informed by leading research and practice and by their own proactive, independent learning.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you can think critically about current issues in business and management, drawing on leading research and practice and your own independent study.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.about: critical evaluation of current research and scholarship
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown conceptual understanding that allows critical evaluation of current research and advanced scholarship in the field or a specialism.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown the conceptual understanding needed to evaluate current research and advanced scholarship critically.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you understand the ideas well enough to judge current research and scholarship in your field critically.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown that they can apply relevant knowledge to a range of complex situations, allowing for its links with other parts of the business or organisation.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has applied relevant knowledge to varied complex situations while accounting for links with other parts of the organisation.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you can use what you know in complex situations, taking account of how one part of an organisation affects the others.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.about: originality in applying knowledge and research practice
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown originality and creativity in applying knowledge, with a practical grasp of how established research and enquiry techniques produce and interpret knowledge in the field.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has applied knowledge with originality and creativity and understands in practice how established research techniques create and interpret knowledge.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown original, creative use of what you know and a practical understanding of how research creates and makes sense of knowledge in your field.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.about: evaluating and joining theory and practice
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown that they can evaluate and integrate theory and practice across many situations.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has evaluated and integrated theory and practice across a wide range of situations.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you can weigh up theory and practice and bring them together in many different situations.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown understanding of how research pushes forward the limits of knowledge.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown understanding of how research extends the boundaries of knowledge.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you understand how research moves knowledge forward.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.about: commitment to global social responsibility and integrity
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown commitment to championing global social responsibility and ethical values and to acting with integrity.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown a commitment to global social responsibility and ethical values and has acted with integrity.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you are committed to social responsibility worldwide, to ethical values and to acting with integrity.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown the ability to take an international view, including the effects of globalisation on business, society and the environment and their ethical implications.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown an international perspective, understanding how globalisation affects organisations, societies and the environment, with its ethical implications.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you can take an international view, including how globalisation affects business, society and the environment and what that means ethically.

statements.appliesTo: holders of a master's degree in business and management at the threshold
statements.about: managing and leading with global social responsibility
statements.paraphrase: Will have shown they can lead and manage with a firm sense of social responsibility worldwide, aware of the conflicting pressures this brings in complex settings.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, every graduate has shown they can lead and manage with a firm sense of worldwide social responsibility, recognising the tensions it creates in complex environments.

forBeneficiary.text: To reach the threshold for the award, you will have shown that you can manage and lead with a strong sense of social responsibility, aware of the tensions this creates in complex settings.
